statement: You are given two arrays nums1 and nums2, each sorted in ascending order, and an integer k between 1 and the total number of elements.
Imagine merging the two arrays into one sorted array. Return the element at position k of that merged array, counting from 1.

Do it without merging, in O(log(min(m, n))) time: binary search on how many of the first k elements come from the shorter array, and accept the split when every element taken is at most every element left behind.

examples.explanation: The merged order begins 1, 2, 4, 9, 10, 13, 14, …, so the 7th element is 14.
The merged order begins −13, −7, −5, −3, …, so the 4th element is −3.
